_comment: The capability table. This is the ONLY file that knows any vendor's flags.
The tick has no branch on runtime anywhere — a runtime is a row, not a code path.
The entry condition for being a first-class Smokin runtime is: it can be started by a
shell command, and it can write a file into a directory. It is NOT 'is one of herdr's
21 kinds' and NOT 'has a hook system'. Codewhale is neither and works fine.
{LINE} is the one-line dispatch prompt. {WT} is the plan root.

claude.note: A per-pane --settings accelerant is NOT shipped: whether it merges or replaces is untested, and if it replaces it would silently disable herdr's own state hook and Grillin's awareness hooks. Open question Q3.

codewhale.verified: headless CONFIRMED returns {"mode":"one-shot","success":true,...}; pane emission CONFIRMED by experiment Q1 — the wrapper trap fires on pane close with rc=129
codewhale.note: Not one of herdr's 21 agent kinds, so herdr cannot classify its lifecycle. Under Smokin that costs nothing: the tick never asks herdr what any agent is doing. Its global-only hooks must never carry a task id — a hook is machine-wide and would fire for every pane.

opencode.verified: installed at ~/.opencode/bin/opencode; headless flag SUSPECTED, not exercised
opencode.note: Its SSE event stream needs a resident subscriber, which is the one thing this design refuses to depend on. Wrapper + reaper only.

codex.verified: NOT INSTALLED on this machine — every field here is SUSPECTED, from vendor docs
codex.note: codex is absent, so smokin doctor reports it MISSING rather than letting a gate that shells out to it exit 127 and read as a clean failure.

aider.note: Untested end to end. Declared so doctor reports it honestly rather than omitting it.
